title: Article 309 — Recruitment and conditions of service of persons serving the Union or a State

content.overview: Article 309 empowers the appropriate Legislature to regulate the recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to public services and posts in connection with the affairs of the Union or of any State by Acts. Until such provision is made, the President (for Union) or the Governor (for a State) may make rules regulating recruitment and conditions of service. Rules so made have effect subject to the provisions of any such Act.
content.glance: Legislature may regulate recruitment and service conditions by law. Until then, President (Union) / Governor (State) may make rules. Rules subject to later Acts.
content.study:
Article 309 is the primary source of legislative and interim executive power over recruitment and conditions of service:
1. Appropriate Legislature may regulate by Act.
2. Until provision is made by Act: President (Union services/posts) or Governor (State services/posts) may make rules.
3. Rules have effect subject to any Act made under the article.

Service rules and recruitment rules derive authority from Article 309 (or from Acts made under it). They must still conform to other constitutional constraints (e.g. Articles 14, 16, 311).

Examination: dual track (Act / rules); President vs Governor; rules subordinate to Acts; link Arts 310–311.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. Appropriate Legislature may regulate recruitment and conditions of service by Act.
2. Until then: President (Union) or Governor (State) may make rules.
3. Rules subject to provisions of any Act under this article.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does Article 309 provide regarding recruitment and conditions of service?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 309 provides that Acts of the appropriate Legislature may regulate the recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to public services and posts in connection with the affairs of the Union or of any State. Until provision in that behalf is made by such Act, the President (in the case of Union services and posts) or the Governor (in the case of State services and posts) may make rules regulating recruitment and conditions of service. Any such rules have effect subject to the provisions of the Act.

examTips: Legislature by Act; interim rules by President/Governor; rules subject to Acts.

keyTakeaways: Art 309: recruitment and service conditions — Acts and interim rules.
